HR@10 against 99 unique negatives measures ranking within a 100-item candidate set. Sampled metrics can reverse model ordering relative to full-catalog metrics, even in expectation. Fixed candidates improve reproducibility and paired comparisons; uniqueness prevents duplicate negatives but does not remove sampling bias. Report gains specifically as pinned sampled-validation gains, without claiming full-catalog improvement. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

For this design, use a paired, dataset-stratified bootstrap: resample 200 users with replacement within each dataset, preserve each user’s outcomes across configurations, and recompute the equally weighted mean of four dataset-level HR differences. Pairing preserves covariance between models. These intervals approximate user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the trained models, fixed candidates and four datasets; they exclude training-seed variability, negative-resampling variability and uncertainty across other datasets. They assume representative, independent users; sparse model disagreements can yield unstable intervals. One changed hit moves dataset HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. [Paired bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)

Selecting the highest score among three configurations on the same validation set creates winner’s-curse optimism; three trials reduce exposure compared with a large search but do not eliminate it. Ordinary bootstrap intervals computed after selection do not automatically provide selection-adjusted coverage. Report all three configurations, per-dataset scores, macro differences and explicitly conditional intervals; count checkpoint selection and earlier adaptive trials as additional search. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged, and reserve the independent held-out evaluation for assessing the selected configuration. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
